tagline: Where East meets West — an Ottoman bazaar beside Austro-Hungarian avenues, on the corner where one shot started World War I.
overview: Sarajevo is Europe's most unusual capital: within one block you pass an Ottoman bazaar of copper craftsmen, a mosque, a Catholic cathedral, an Orthodox church and a synagogue — the 'Jerusalem of Europe.'

History pivots on a street corner: the Latin Bridge's north end is where Gavrilo Princip shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914, tipping Europe into WWI. The 1990s siege — 1,425 days, the longest in modern history — is remembered at the Tunnel of Hope museum.

Speed's 2024 tour streamed from Sarajevo. The city today is famously welcoming — Baščaršija's lanes serve Bosnian coffee in copper sets, ćevapi grills scent the air, and the 1984 Olympic mountains still ring the valley.

funFacts.title: WHERE EAST MEETS WEST
funFacts.text: The Ferhadija line literally marks where Ottoman architecture hands off to Austro-Hungarian.

funFacts.title: THE SHOT THAT STARTED WWI
funFacts.text: Princip's assassination of Franz Ferdinand happened at the Latin Bridge in 1914.

funFacts.title: THE LONGEST SIEGE
funFacts.text: The 1992–95 siege lasted 1,425 days — the Tunnel of Hope museum preserves the lifeline under the airport.

funFacts.title: FOUR FAITHS, ONE BLOCK
funFacts.text: Mosque, cathedral, Orthodox church and synagogue stand within a few hundred metres.

funFacts.title: COPPER STREET
funFacts.text: Kazandžiluk lane's coppersmiths have hammered coffee sets for five centuries.

funFacts.title: OLYMPIC CITY
funFacts.text: Sarajevo hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics — the bobsled track remains as graffiti concrete.

funFacts.title: BOSNIAN COFFEE
funFacts.text: Coffee is served in a džezva with rahat lokum — a ritual, not a drink.

funFacts.title: SEBILJ
funFacts.text: The wooden fountain in the bazaar square is the city's symbol — drinking it means you'll return.

funFacts.title: THE AVAZ TOWER
funFacts.text: The twisted skyscraper marks the postwar rebuild's ambition.

funFacts.title: COLDEST LEGACY
funFacts.text: Abandoned Olympic venues became poignant ruins — now partly restored for visitors.
